title: Anthropic Just Fell Below Its IPO Price, but Here's What the Stock Could Be Worth in 2030
summary: By Geoffrey Seiler – Nov 24, 2026 at 12:44PM EST 10 stocks we like better than Anthropic › Much like SpaceX ( SPCX -5.65% ) before it, Anthropic 's ( ANT -6.54% ) newly public stock has struggled out of the gate, falling below its IPO price as I write this. However, the company is experiencing parabolic revenue growth, and its early trading action isn't necessarily indicative of where the stock may trade by the end of 2030. Let's look at how this AI stock could more than quadruple from here over the next few years, and the risks it may face in reaching that target. Anthropic has grown to become one of the most important frontier AI labs after being founded just five years ago. The company has grown its revenue rapidly by catering largely to enterprises. Nearly 80% of Anthropic's revenue comes from usage fees that developers pay the company for access to its models and applications. This is a pay-for-intelligence consumption model where customers pay based on which model is used and how many input and output tokens the model processes. A token is a unit of data that an AI model processes to generate a response. Output tokens generally are more expensive than input tokens. The other 20% of its revenue comes from subscriptions. Through the first nine months of the year, Anthropic saw its revenue surge 1,200% to $33.24 billion. Revenue has been growing parabolically, with Q3 revenue up more than 12 times to $17 billion from $1.4 billion a year ago and nearly 50% sequentially from $11.6 billion in Q2. Anthropic's success comes from a combination of its enterprise focus and its shift to offering applications. The company has seen huge success with Claude Code, the company's agentic coding tool that can write code and fix errors while navigating codebases. Meanwhile, much of its future growth will likely center around offering new applications on top of its models, with this being a new way to drive token consumption. It's already started rolling out new capabilities, including Computer Use, which allows its Claude model to see a screen, interact with software the way a human would, and carry out tasks directly. Building out new and better AI models comes with the need for a lot of AI infrastructure spending, and Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in future commitments. That's a huge amount of money that the company is going to have to raise over the next several years. One thing the company is doing to try to lower future costs is basically help commoditize AI…

title: Anthropic shares fall below IPO price, a worrying sign for AI startups
summary: Anthropic’s stock fell below its IPO price of $83 , trading as low as $76 a share by midday Tuesday, down nearly 12% from Monday’s close. Falling below the IPO price is often seen as a negative signal because underwriters typically price offerings at a discount to their expected trading value. The AI industry has been eagerly watching how Anthropic’s shares trade, with VCs and other observers saying its performance could serve as a barometer for how public market investors value the sector. The dramatic slump comes less than a week after Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq at $111.50 a share . If its shares continue to trade poorly in the coming weeks, the slide could put pressure on private startup valuations and weaken IPO prospects for other AI companies. Anthropic isn’t the only AI stock selling off on Tuesday. Nvidia fell more than 7% by midday, giving back some of the more than 30%-plus gain it posted Monday after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO.
